#167 Stage 3 assumption A7. PostsController runs before_action :require_login on #index, and a static page cannot enforce it -- the ZigBase rules on the posts collection do (listRule @public, createRule @request.auth.id != ""). `public` is the operator saying so out loud rather than the migration shipping a guarded page silently. It does NOT settle this route: the two `retain` answers above outrank it, so /posts stays on Rails and no page is written for it (ruling S20). Deleting those two is what makes this answer visible, and rails-presentation.sh runs exactly that variant.
The source route has no deterministic browser example for parity, so the full-stack fixture keeps it blocked instead of claiming an unproved SPA migration.

#167 Stage 3. GET /feed renders `Post.all` as JSON, which is exactly what the backend document's `listPosts` operation returns -- so the route is bound to it rather than kept on Rails. It is also the one route assumption A2 bites on: a user-facing GET the handoff calls `backend` is UNACCOUNTED until an operation is chosen, so without this answer the run cannot reach `complete` however everything else is answered.

#167 Stage 3 assumption A5 folds the sign-in and sign-up forms into one question, because the answer to both is a single ZigBase auth collection. `users` is the artifact: it is the only auth collection in backend/openapi.json (an auth collection is recognisable ONLY by its create schema carrying both `password` and `passwordConfirm`), and naming any other name is refused. The answer scaffolds ONE components/AuthForm.island.tsx told apart by a `mode` prop, lib/zb.ts, and the three endpoints the document has no ids for -- authWithPassword, logout, createUsers.

the signed-OUT half of the nav (`unless current_user`). the signed-IN half. The route's note names which of the pair was folded into the other.

`current_user.email` inside that half; the AuthStatus island reads it from the browser's auth store instead. Note what is NOT answered here: the `button_to "Sign out"` beside it raises its own RAILS_BACKEND_ENDPOINT, and the AuthStatus island replaces the whole region including that control, so the region's answer is the only one it needs -- answering it separately is what rails-presentation.sh's negative arm covers.

the `@user&.errors&.any?` summary. The bound AuthForm renders the backend's own field errors where this rendered Rails', so the region is answered by the island rather than retained: this is the validation-presentation half of the backend boundary.

the `full_messages.each do |m|` loop inside that same summary. Answering it `island` is also what closes #181 here: the unbound `|m|` block local never reaches the converter at all once the island owns the region, so the route no longer carries an id-less `rails:unmapped local` that no answer could settle.
